aphis_jun.title: USDA Confirms Presence of New World Screwworm in the United States (APHIS, June 3, 2026)

aphis_az.title: USDA Confirms New World Screwworm in Arizona (APHIS, Oct 28, 2026)

dtn_oct.title: New World Screwworm Found in Arizona as USDA Reopens Border Trade (DTN, Oct 30, 2026)

nobel.title: Hermann J. Muller, Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 1946

papers.title: Bushland & Hopkins 1951, J Econ Entomol 44:725 (doi:10.1093/jee/44.5.725); Knipling 1955, J Econ Entomol 48:459 (doi:10.1093/jee/48.4.459); Baumhover et al. 1955, J Econ Entomol 48:462 (doi:10.1093/jee/48.4.462)

facts.claim: June 3, 2026: screwworm larvae found in the navel of a 3-week-old calf in Zavala County, Texas.
facts.source_sentence: a 3-week-old bovine ... larvae were identified in its umbilical area (Zavala County, Texas; June 3, 2026)

facts.claim: Screwworm maggots feed on living tissue of warm-blooded animals and attack healthy tissue.
facts.source_sentence: a species of parasitic blowfly whose larvae (maggots) feed on living tissue of warm-blooded animals ... screwworm maggots are unusual because they attack healthy tissue.

facts.claim: Sterile flies eradicated the screwworm from the US in 1966.
facts.source_sentence: The sterile-insect approach eradicated the screwworm from the U.S. in 1966.

facts.claim: The US and Mexico bred and released more than 94 billion sterile flies from 1962 to 1975.
facts.source_sentence: The US and Mexico bred and released more than 94 billion sterile flies from 1962 to 1975.

facts.claim: Females lay 250-500 eggs in exposed flesh, near wounds or newborns' navels.
facts.source_sentence: Screwworm females lay 250–500 eggs in the exposed flesh of warm-blooded animals ... near wounds ... but also near the navel of newborns

facts.claim: Disturbed larvae burrow or 'screw' deeper, hence the name; damage can kill the host and the wound attracts more flies.
facts.source_sentence: Should the wound be disturbed during this time, the larvae burrow or "screw" deeper into the flesh, hence the larva's common name. The maggots can cause severe tissue damage or even death to the host. ... the damaged tissue attracts more flies.

facts.claim: It infests wild and domestic animals, and less frequently birds and humans.
facts.source_sentence: The New World screwworm fly infests wild and domestic animals, and less frequently birds and humans.

facts.claim: Before US elimination it could spread as far as the Canadian border in favorable years.
facts.source_sentence: Before its elimination in the US, the screwworm fly could spread as far as the Canadian border in favorable years.

facts.claim: In the 1930s ARS scientists Edward Knipling and Raymond Bushland looked for control methods beyond treating wounds.
facts.source_sentence: In the 1930's ARS scientists Edward F. Knipling and Raymond C. Bushland turned their attention ...

facts.claim: Females mate only once and keep the sperm for life; the sterile insect technique exploits this.
facts.source_sentence: Females copulate only once and retain the male's sperm for life, a fact which has been exploited in eradication programs using the sterile insect technique.

facts.claim: Fertile wild females would mate with mass-reared sterilized males released into infested areas.
facts.source_sentence: Fertile females would mate with sterilized males mass-reared in insectaries and released into infested areas.

facts.claim: A colleague pointed Knipling to a book by Nobel laureate H. J. Muller on using radiation to alter insects' genetic material.
facts.source_sentence: colleague Arthur W. Lindquist recommended to Knipling a book by Nobel laureate H. J. Muller ... discussed use of radiation to alter the genetic material of insects

facts.claim: At Kerrville, Texas, Bushland used a nearby Army medical unit's X-ray equipment; within 6 months a sterilizing dose was shown.
facts.source_sentence: tests at Kerrville, Texas ... a nearby U.S. Army medical unit with suitable x-ray equipment. In just 6 months, it was handily demonstrated that 2,500 to 5,000 roentgens of x-rays would sterilize screwworm pupae.

facts.claim: Bushland and Hopkins published experiments with X-ray-sterilized screwworm flies in 1951.
facts.source_sentence: Bushland RC, Hopkins DE. Experiments with Screw-Worm Flies Sterilized by X-Rays. J Econ Entomol 1951;44(5):725.

facts.claim: A first field test on Sanibel, a 20-square-mile Florida island, confirmed the theory; the team then sought a more conclusive site.
facts.source_sentence: First, a field test on Sanibel, the 20-square-mile Florida island, confirmed the theory. (NAL: the research staff began looking for test sites that might prove more conclusive than Sanibel.)

facts.claim: On Curaçao (1954), about a thousand sterile flies per square mile were released each week by airplane.
facts.source_sentence: So a thousand sterile flies per square mile were released each week by airplane. (NAL: releases from March 1954 into January 1955.)

facts.claim: After three weeks about 70 percent of egg masses found were sterile; within about two months no fertile eggs could be found.
facts.source_sentence: After just three weeks ... about 70 percent of new egg cases found were sterile. (NAL: Within about two months, fertile eggs could no longer be found on the island.)

facts.claim: In 1955 Knipling published the theory and Baumhover et al. published the Curaçao result.
facts.source_sentence: Knipling EF. Possibilities of Insect Control or Eradication Through the Use of Sexually Sterile Males. J Econ Entomol 1955;48(4):459. Baumhover AH et al. Screw-Worm Control Through Release of Sterilized Flies. J Econ Entomol 1955;48(4):462.

facts.claim: From 1958 to 1960 it was eliminated from the Southeastern and then the Southwestern US.
facts.source_sentence: From 1958 to 1960, the species was eliminated from the Southeastern and then the Southwestern United States.

facts.claim: Since 1991 Mexico and several Central American countries have been declared free of screwworm.
facts.source_sentence: Since 1991, Mexico and several countries in Central America have been declared free of screwworm.

facts.claim: A Panama facility maintains a barrier zone at the Darién Gap with weekly releases of up to 100 million sterile flies.
facts.source_sentence: In 2003 a screwworm production facility in Panama ... maintains the barrier zone at the Darien Gap ... weekly sterile New World screwworm fly releases of up to 100 million insects.

facts.claim: A 2016 outbreak in the Florida Keys infested endangered Key deer; it was declared neutralized in March 2017.
facts.source_sentence: an isolated outbreak occurred in the Florida Keys ... in autumn of 2016 [Key deer] ... the outbreak was declared as neutralized in March 2017.

facts.claim: In December 2024 screwworm re-emerged in southern Mexico, indicating the Panama barrier had been breached.
facts.source_sentence: in December 2024, the screwworm was reported to have re-emerged in Southern Mexico, indicating that the protective barrier in Panama had been breached.

facts.claim: The border closed to Mexican cattle trade in July 2025 as the fly spread north in Mexico.
facts.source_sentence: The Mexico-U.S. border closed to cattle trade in July 2025 because NWS was spreading north in Mexico.

facts.claim: Cases were found less than 70 miles from the border (Sept 2025), then within 31 miles (May 2026).
facts.source_sentence: In September 2025, a case ... less than 70 miles from the US-Mexico border. In May 2026, another case ... within 31 miles (50 km) from the US-Mexico border.

facts.claim: By Oct 30, 2026: 71 total US cases, including dogs and a cat, in Texas, New Mexico and Arizona (first Arizona case Oct 28).
facts.source_sentence: The U.S. has 71 total NWS cases ... Oct. 28: a dog and a domestic cat in New Mexico ... (APHIS: a dog in Cochise County, Arizona ... the first detection of NWS in Arizona)

facts.claim: Sterile flies are being released over the Texas outbreak area.
facts.source_sentence: 4 million sterile flies per week already being released aerially in the area ... ground release chambers are being deployed

facts.claim: A US sterile fly plant at Moore Air Base, Edinburg, Texas, is expected to run by end of 2026: 100 million flies in stage 1, 300 million by end of 2028.
facts.source_sentence: USDA's domestic sterile fly production facility at the Moore Air Base in Edinburg, Texas ... will initially produce 100 million sterile NWS flies during stage 1 ... 300 million by stage 2 at the end of 2028 ... expected to be up and running by the end of 2026.

facts.claim: Check pets and livestock for wounds and larvae; report suspected cases; the food supply is safe.
facts.source_sentence: check pets and livestock for draining or enlarging wounds ... larvae or eggs ... Suspected cases should be reported ... The U.S. food supply is safe
